properties.description:

near Whiteriver, moving northeast at 40 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and half dollar size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

Whiteriver, North Fork, Canyon Day, Rainbow City, Seven Mile, East
Fork, Turkey Creek, Fort Apache, Kinishba Ruins, Whiteriver Airport
and Round Top Mountain.

windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Bristol Bay Coast
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 22 at 1:56AM AKDT until October 24 at 7:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Water levels most likely around 1.0 to 2.0 feet above
the normal highest tide line, with highest water levels
expected near Togiak.

* WHERE...Northern Bristol Bay Coast.

* WHEN...10 AM Friday to 7AM Saturday

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low lying areas. Coastal
erosion is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A Bering front arrives to the Southwest
Alaska coast Friday morning, bringing a prolonged period of
strong southerly winds towards the coast. These winds will
result in elevated water levels and high surf. This period of
winds will coincide with two tidal cycles and push water
levels 1.0 to 2.0 feet above the normal highest tide line.
Water levels are expected to quickly drop off Saturday morning
as winds decrease, alleviating coastal concerns.
properties.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

NWSheadline: HIGH SURF ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 10 AM FRIDAY TO 7 AM AKDT SATURDAY

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 22 at 1:56AM AKDT until October 24 at 1:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal flooding and high surf conditions are possible
due to 35 to 50 mph winds with gusts up to 75 mph.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kipnuk, Kwigillingok
and Kongiganak.

* WHEN...8 AM Friday through 1 AM Saturday, particularly around
high tides near 10 AM and 10 PM Friday.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely scenario is for water
levels to be 2.0 to 3.0 ft above the normal high tide line,
which would be similar to the water levels during the August
18 2024 storm. While unlikely, the worst case scenario for
Kipnuk is for water levels to be 3.5 to 4.0 feet above the
normal high tide line, while the worst case for Kwigillingok
is 4.0 to 5.0 feet above the normal high tide line. We are
closely monitoring this storm. In the meantime, please have a
plan in place.
properties.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 22 at 5:49AM EDT until October 22 at 11:00PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...In Delaware, Inland Sussex and Delaware Beaches. In
New Jersey, Ocean and Coastal Ocean.

* WHEN...Until 11 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most
vulnerable roads in coastal and bayside communities, and along
inland tidal waterways. Some partial or full road closures are
possible.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 22 at 2:32AM MST until October 22 at 8:15AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
At 332 AM MDT, a river gauge on Chine Creek within Canyon de Chelly
National Monument reported water levels had fallen below flood stage.
However, flooding will remain a threat in areas downstream of Canyon
de Chelly through the morning hours. Flash flooding is already
occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of Chine Creek.

For Chinle Creek at Chinle:
At 3:00am the stage was 3.4 feet.
Flood Stage is 4.0 feet.
Impacts:
At 3.6 feet: Chinle Creek becomes impassable to recreational
vehicles.
At 4.0 feet: Water begins to encroach upon structures just upstream
of the Highway 64 bridge near the Canyon de Chelly welcome center.
At 4.3 feet: Flooding to homes and residences in Chinle on left bank
downstream from Highway 64 bridge.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Chinle, Canyon De Chelly National Monument and Mummy Cave Overlook.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Junction Overlook, White House Overlook, Antelope House Overlook and
Face Rock Overlook.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Chinle Wash, Coyote Wash, Muerto, Canyon del, Sheep Dip Creek,
Black Rock Canyon and Nazlini Wash.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.
